newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares lose little despite Dow plunge.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares lose little despite Dow plunge.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange index ended down 8.91 points, or 0.28 percent, at 3,120.20 but brokers said it reflected strength in the face of sharp falls in other regional markets.

"The index dropped only 10 points and compare that to the U.S overnight. It shows people are looking forward to 1997 with average earnings growth of about 30 percent year on year," Lawrence Lownang of Sun Hung Kai Securities said.
On Thursday, U.S. blue chips dropped like a stone in the last hour of trading, shedding nearly 100 points in the biggest point loss since mid-July.
Asian bourses in Tokyo, Hong Kong, Jakarta, Seoul and Bangkok followed suit but the Philippine market was stable, mainly because of buying in utility companies, brokers said.
Among the gainers were Digital Telecommunications and Manila Electric Co. But the index was pulled down by heavyweights like Ayala Corp, Ayala Land and PLDT.
Trading volumes were lower at around 2.0 billion pesos compared to the average 2.5 billion.
Sun Hung Kai's Lownang said the Philippine market's resilience was "quite spectacular when you consider the other markets in the region."
Lownang said he expected very narrow movement in Philippine stocks until the year-end.
